# Privacy and Your Data

Purpose: explain in plain language what Longstead stores, where it is stored, which network connections it can make, how to delete your data, and how to move to a new device.

This page describes how the app behaves. The legal text is in the app under **Settings > About & legal > Privacy Policy**. Publisher: Core Hermit. Contact: wavypix@gmail.com.

## The short version

- No account, no sign-in, no ads, no analytics, no tracking.
- Your profile, accounts, plans and chats are stored **only on your device**.
- All calculations are done **on your device**, and by default so are all AI answers. If you connect your own model server, your questions go to that server (see below).
- On its own, the app contacts a third-party site only when you download an AI model (huggingface.co) and, if you enter your own tax-data feed address, to check that address for updated tax tables. Neither sends your plan data. If you connect your own model server, the app also talks to that server.

## What is stored, and where

Everything the app saves lives in one folder called `RetirementPlanner` inside the app's **Application Support** location.

| Platform | Location |
| --- | --- |
| iPhone / iPad | Inside the app's private storage (`Library/Application Support/RetirementPlanner`). Other apps cannot read it. Deleting the app deletes it. |
| Mac | `~/Library/Application Support/RetirementPlanner` (the **Library** folder is hidden in Finder: in Finder choose **Go > Go to Folder...** and paste the path). Your plans, accounts and chats are stored on an encrypted disk image inside it (`Data.sparsebundle`, AES-256, a macOS feature). The app creates a random key, keeps it in your login Keychain, mounts the image while the app is open and unmounts it when you quit. If the key is lost (for example you erase the Keychain or move to a new Mac without a Keychain backup), the data cannot be opened or recovered. Turning on FileVault in System Settings protects the rest of your disk too. |

| Item in that folder | What it holds | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `retirement.sqlite` (and its companion files with the same start) | Your plans, profile, accounts, chat messages, and saved analyses | The main database. On a Mac it is kept inside `Data.sparsebundle`, an AES-256 encrypted disk image (see below), so you will not see it loose in this folder. |
| `settings.json` | Your settings, the list of installed models, text size, and any tax-data feed address you entered | Plain text. An API key for your own model server is not kept here; it goes in the Keychain. |
| `Models/` | Downloaded AI model files, one folder per model, named like `mlx-community__Qwen3.5-4B-MLX-4bit` | Several gigabytes in total. |
| `tax-data/` | Tax tables downloaded from your own feed address, only if you set one up | The app also contains built-in tables. |
| `network-audit.json` | The network audit log (see below) | Holds up to 200 entries. |
| `errors.json` | A short note if a downloaded model failed to load at launch | Created only if that happens. |

What the main database contains: the name, ages, filing status, state, spending and Social Security figures you entered; every account's name, type, institution, balance, contribution, match, return and notes; your chat messages; and a saved copy of each question and answer (the "analyses").

### Backups

The app marks its `RetirementPlanner` folder as **excluded from backup**. In practice that means:

- An iCloud or computer backup of your iPhone or iPad does **not** include your plans. If you restore a backup onto a new device, or erase the device, your plan data will not come with it.
- On a Mac, the same flag normally keeps the folder out of Time Machine backups.

So **export your plans** (below) if you want a copy. The in-app Privacy Policy says iOS may include app data in your own backups; the app's actual setting is the exclusion described here.

## What the AI sees

By default the AI runs on the device (Apple's built-in model or a downloaded model). What each advisor receives is described in [AI_AND_MODELS.md](AI_AND_MODELS.md); the Retirement Planner gets only a pass/fail check of the required inputs plus your question. That text is processed on the device and is never uploaded by the app. Private Cloud Compute, Apple's server option, is switched off and cannot be selected. The app contains no cloud AI service of its own.

**If you connect your own model server** (Ollama, LM Studio or another OpenAI-compatible server), an advisor set to use it sends what the model sees to that server. A local address (`localhost`, `127.x`, `*.local`, `10.x`, `172.16` to `172.31.x`, `192.168.x`) is treated as your own computer or network. Any other address shows a warning that your questions and plan details would be sent to that server. The server's own privacy practices apply.

If you turn on Apple Intelligence in iOS or macOS, the operating system manages Apple's model, including any Apple model files it downloads. That is done by Apple's system, not by this app.

The **Listen** button reads answers aloud using your device's built-in voice, on the device.

## Network connections

The app has no server of its own and sends nothing to its publisher. These are all of the connections the app can make:

| Host | When | What is requested | What is sent about you |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **huggingface.co** | Only when you tap **Download** on a model (and, if a model is listed as installed but its folder is missing, when the app tries to load it). | The list of files for the model, then each file. Hugging Face may serve file contents from its own file-hosting domains after a redirect. | Nothing from your plan. Hugging Face sees your IP address and which model you asked for. |
| **Your own tax-data address** | Only if you enter one in Settings > Tax data (none by default): about every 30 days when "Allow yearly tax-data updates" is on, and when you tap **Check now**. | Five public tax-table files: `federal_brackets.json`, `state_brackets.json`, `standard_deductions.json`, `capital_gains.json`, `rmd_table.json`. | Nothing from your plan. That host sees your IP address. |
| **Your own model server** | Only if you connect one in Settings > Your own model server, or the app finds Ollama at `http://localhost:11434` on its own (once at launch and when a chat opens). | Chat requests to the server, and requests for its models and their sizes and abilities. | Your questions and plan details, as described above. The server's owner sees them. With the default local addresses this stays on your computer or network. |
| **Links you tap** | Support email (opens your Mail app) and the policy links inside the legal documents (open your browser). | n/a | Whatever that app or site receives. |

By default the app makes no tax-data requests. If you added a feed address, turn off **Allow yearly tax-data updates** or clear the address to stop them. You can avoid the model host entirely by not downloading models (Apple's on-device model needs no download). If you do not want the app to talk to a model server, choose **Disconnect** in Settings > Your own model server, or tap **Use Apple's built-in model instead** in the chat header. On iPhone and iPad, iOS shows a Local Network permission prompt when a server on the network is used.

### The Network audit log

**Settings > Privacy > Network audit log** lists the requests the app makes: the start of each model download (`huggingface.co`, purpose `model_download`; one entry per download, not per file) if you use your own feed address, each tax-data request (host, path, result, size, purpose `tax_data_update`), and each request to your own model server, with a purpose text. Newest first, up to 200 entries, with a **Clear** button. The table above is the complete list of what the app can connect to.

## Sharing and exports

The app shares something only when you ask it to. **Export plan...** (in Profile) creates a `.retplan` file containing your plan's name and description, profile (name, ages, filing status, state, spending, Social Security, risk tolerance) and all accounts (names, types, institutions, balances, contributions, notes). It is **plain, unencrypted text**. Anyone who gets the file can read it. Store it somewhere private and delete it when you no longer need it. The file also carries a second copy of the same data in the layout used by the earlier desktop version of the app.

You can also export one advisor conversation (chat menu > Export conversation...) as Markdown, shared text or PDF; that contains the questions and answers in that thread, which may include figures from your profile. A plan export does not include chat messages, saved analyses, settings, or downloaded models.

## Deleting data

| To delete | How |
| --- | --- |
| An account | Swipe it in **Accounts** and tap Delete. |
| One advisor's chat for the active plan | Open the chat, tap the menu at the top right, **Clear thread**. This removes the messages; saved analyses for the plan remain. |
| A plan and everything in it (profile, accounts, chats, analyses) | iPhone: **Profile > Plan management > Reset plan** (deletes the active plan). Mac/iPad: also **Projects**: swipe Delete, or open the project and **Delete project**. This cannot be undone. |
| A downloaded model | **Settings > Manage models > Remove**, or **Settings > Installed model storage > Delete**. |
| The network audit log | **Settings > Privacy > Network audit log > Clear**. |
| A downloaded tax-data update | Only applies if you used your own feed. **Erase all data** or deleting the app removes it; on a Mac you can also delete the `tax-data` folder. |
| Everything (iPhone, iPad, Mac) | **Settings > Your data > Erase all data...**. Deletes all plans, accounts, chats, analyses, settings and downloaded models in the app's own storage, and resets the setup wizard. On a Mac it does not touch a shared `~/.cache/huggingface`. Deleting the app (iPhone) also removes everything. |
| Everything on Mac, by hand | Quit the app, move it to the Trash, then delete the `RetirementPlanner` folder shown above. See [MAC_INSTALLATION.md](MAC_INSTALLATION.md). |

When you delete a plan, the app deletes its saved analyses with it. Because the database may keep freed space until it is reused, deleting the app or folder is the only way to be certain nothing remains.

## Moving to a new device

Because plan data is not included in device backups, move your plans yourself:

1. On the old device, open **Profile > Plan management > Export plan...** for each plan you want. Save the `.retplan` files to Files, iCloud Drive, or AirDrop them.
2. Install Longstead on the new device.
3. In **Profile > Plan management > Import plan...**, choose each file. Each import creates a new plan and makes it the active one.
4. Re-enter your settings (they are not in the file), and download your AI models again from **Settings > Manage models** if you want them.

Chat history and saved analyses are not carried over.
